extracted.intended_audience: Journalists (especially those who don't normally cover the LGBTQ+ community); mainstream and LGBTQ+ reporters
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for journalists on assessing news value and maintaining fairness when covering LGBTQ+ topics — with particular attention to avoiding sensationalism during ratings-driven sweeps periods. Helps reporters decide when a story (e.g., public sex or arrests) is genuinely newsworthy versus exploitative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliver balanced LGBT-related stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Tips on how journalists can deliver more balanced LGBT-related stories during sweeps (and year round).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice is drawn from media experts and NLGJA members; intended to help reporters produce coverage that is not inaccurate or unbalanced. The toolkit offers story ideas and new ways of thinking for reporters experienced and inexperienced in covering LGBTQ life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess newsworthiness versus sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether a story (especially sex- or scandal-driven coverage) is actually newsworthy or merely sensationalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples to consider: public sex stories run during sweeps and newspaper stories about arrests for public lewdness. Ask whether events like men meeting for sex in a public restroom are inherently newsworthy or are being presented for sensational appeal. These are debatable judgments, but reporters should weigh news value carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid exploiting sweeps/rating cycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about allowing sweeps-month pressure for ratings (celebrities, sex, etc.) to drive coverage that results in inaccurate or unbalanced reporting about sexual minorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the annual quest for broadcast ratings supremacy can produce distorted coverage; print outlets can also be guilty. Keep in mind points of responsible journalism during sweeps and throughout the year to prevent sensationalized portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use contextual judgment on law-enforcement-related coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting on arrests (e.g., public lewdness), evaluate the broader context before making the incident a news story about a community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The toolkit flags police arrests for public lewdness as a common example where reporters should consider whether the incident reflects a broader public-interest issue or risks stigmatizing sexual minorities without sufficient context.
